def generate_toc_id(slug):
        """
        This function generates a unique id for a heading.
        Input-Output Arguments
        :param slug: String. The slug of the heading.
        :return: String. The unique id for the heading.
        """
        if heading_id:
            return heading_id(slug)
        else:
            return slug

    def generate_toc_item(tokens, index):
        """
        This function generates a table of contents item.
        Input-Output Arguments
        :param tokens: List. The list of tokens.
        :param index: Integer. The index of the heading.
        :return: Dict. The table of contents item.
        """
        title = tokens[index]["children"][0]["children"][0]
        level = tokens[index]["level"]
        slug = tokens[index]["attrs"]["id"]
        return {
            "title": title,
            "level": level,
            "slug": slug,
            "id": generate_toc_id(slug),
        }

            level = tokens[index]["level"]

                    md.env["toc"] = []
                md.env["toc"].append(item)
                add_toc_items(tokens, index + 1)
        else:
            add_toc_items(tokens, index + 1)

def _add_toc_hook(state, tokens, idx):
        """
        This function is used to add TOC items into the state.env.
        Input-Output Arguments
        :param state: Dict. The state of the Markdown instance.
        :param tokens: List. The tokens of the Markdown instance.
        :param idx: Integer. The index of the token in the tokens.
        :return: No return values.
        """
        token = tokens[idx]
        if token['type'] != 'heading_open':
            return
        level = int(token['tag'][1])
        if level < min_level or level > max_level:
            return
        title = tokens[idx + 2]['content']
        if heading_id is not None:
            title = heading_id(title)
        title = striptags(title)
        state.env.append({'level': level, 'title': title, 'id': token['attrSet']['id']})

        This function walks through the model graphs and yields their nodes. It uses a generator to yield the nodes of the model graphs.
        Input-Output Arguments
        :param graphs: Iterable of TensorVariable. The graphs to walk.
        :param stop_at_vars: Optional set of TensorVariable. A set of variables at which the walk will terminate. Defaults to None.
        :param expand_fn: Callable function. A function that returns the next variable(s) to be traversed. Defaults to a lambda function that returns an empty list.
        :return: Generator of TensorVariable. A generator that yields the nodes of the model graphs.
        """
        visited = set()
        stack = list(graphs)
        while stack:
            var = stack.pop()
            if var in visited:
                continue
            visited.add(var)
            if stop_at_vars and var in stop_at_vars:
                return
            yield var
            stack.extend(expand_fn(var))

    return _walk_model(graphs, stop_at_vars, expand_fn)

    metadata = data.get("metadata", {})
    defaults = data.get("defaults", {})
    queries = data.get("queries", {})

    # Create instances of QueryMetadata, QueryDefaults, and Query objects
    query_metadata = QueryMetadata(**metadata)
    query_defaults = QueryDefaults(**defaults)
    query_collection = QueryCollection(
        file_name=yaml_file,
        metadata=query_metadata,
        defaults=query_defaults,
        sources={},
    )

    # Create instances of Query objects and add them to the QueryCollection
    for query_name, query_data in queries.items():
        query_args = QueryArgs(**query_data.get("args", {}))
        query_parameters = query_data.get("parameters", {})
        query_metadata = query_data.get("metadata", {})
        query = Query(
            description=query_data.get("description", ""),
            args=query_args,
            parameters=query_parameters,
            metadata=query_metadata,
        )

    def expand_column(col: pd.Series, name: str, prefix: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        This function expands a single column into separate columns with a prefix. It checks if the values in the column are of the specified types and expands them into separate columns with a prefix based on the original column name.
        Input-Output Arguments
        :param col: pd.Series. The column to be expanded.
        :param name: str. The name of the column to be expanded.
        :param prefix: str. The prefix to be used for the expanded columns.
        :return: pd.DataFrame. The DataFrame with the expanded columns.
        """
        if col.dtype in types:
            expanded = pd.json_normalize(col.apply(lambda x: x if isinstance(x, dict) else {name: x}))
            expanded.columns = [f"{prefix}.{x}" for x in expanded.columns]
            return expanded
        return pd.DataFrame()

    expanded = pd.DataFrame()
    for col_name, col in df.iteritems():
        expanded = pd.concat([expanded, expand_column(col, col_name, col_name)], axis=1)
    return expanded
